title: Enterprise Evolution Playbook — Tier Transition Checklist & QBR Opportunity Map
body:
Purpose:
This working playbook captures a repeatable approach for Customer Success to identify, validate, and close expansion motions that move customers from hosted usage into Redwood Dedicated, Private deployment, or premium SLA add-ons. It is designed to be used inside QBRs and renewal cycles as a decisioning and prioritization tool.

High-level objectives (what a successful transition looks like):
- Move 1–3 high-value customers per quarter from hosted->dedicated OR hosted->private, or secure premium SLA add-ons for enterprise accounts.
- Achieve predictable TTV (time-to-value) for Dedicated of <10 weeks for standard lifts; <14 weeks for Private (VPC/on-prem) with customer infra readiness.
- Maintain NPS delta >= +6 after migration (technical onboarding and success plan).

Signals & opportunity scoring (quick sniff test during QBR):
- Usage signals: sustained 4+ months of >250M tokens/month or high-concurrency bursts causing throttling.
- Performance/latency pain: repeated incidents or backlog during peak windows, visible in tracing/Console metrics.
- Data isolation or compliance asks: SOC2 + regulatory requirements, data residency, or audit/KMS needs.
- Cost/efficiency: customer requests per-token cost forecast or quantization/throughput trade discussions.
- Strategic alignment: product roadmap dependence on predictable inference, legal/contractual constraints preventing hosted usage.

Opportunity scorecard (simple):
- Usage (0-4), Stability (0-3), Security/Compliance (0-3), Strategic Fit (0-2), Contract Status (0-2) => >8 candidate for outreach.

QBR Play — agenda template (45–60m) to surface expansion motion:
1) Executive check-in (5m) — top business outcomes since last QBR
2) Health snapshot (10m) — usage, latency, error trends, spend forecast; highlight capacity/tier pinch points
3) Opportunity map (15m) — present Dedicated/Private/SLA options with tailored benefits and tradeoffs (see offer matrix below)
4) Technical feasibility & timeline (10m) — ask infra owners for network/KMS readiness; identify blockers
5) Commercial next steps & approvals (5–10m) — outline contract cadence, pilot terms, success criteria
6) Action items & owners (5m)

Renewal & Tracking primitives (lightweight, usable in a sheet):
- columns: account, ARR, current_plan, usage_monthly_tokens, opportunity_type (dedicated/private/sla), score, QBR_date, technical_ready (yes/no), legal_ready (yes/no), pilot_start_target, commercial_owner, cs_owner, next_action, notes
- triage filter: score >=9 puts account into "expansion cadence" (weekly touch + technical discovery)

Technical validation checklist (to run ASAP after signal):
- Confirm peak concurrency and seq length distribution (app dev).
- Collect representative model(s) and sample prompts, tokenization profile.
- Network checklist: VPN/VPC peering window, firewall rules, egress allowances.
- KMS/HSM requirements: verify key rotation and separation-of-duties needs.
- Data residency and logging retention: confirm minimum retention bound and audit needs.
- Integration test plan: SDKs, streaming, function calling, fallback routing policies.
- Pilot success criteria: latency p99 target, throughput target, error budget, cost per 1M tokens target.

Commercial packaging & sample offers (flexible templates to customize in quotes):
- Dedicated Basic: reserved capacity units, moderate burst, standard SLA (99.5), 12 month term, onboarding credits for 2 weeks of free pilot.
- Dedicated Plus: higher reserved capacity, accelerated SLOs (99.9 for p50/p90), priority support, optional autoscale buffer.
- Private Starter: private control plane + VPC peering, 6-week onboarding, baseline audit package.
- Private Enterprise: on-prem option or air-gapped bundle, HSM integration, extended compliance pack, 24x7 enterprise support, 12–18 week deployment path.
- SLA Add-on: attachable to any plan — incident q/o <15 min, guaranteed fallback routing, extended telemetry retention, dedicated AM.

Commercial negotiation heuristics (CS cheat sheet):
- If customer cites cost, show unit economics: per-token hosted vs. amortized Dedicated cost at their sustained usage. Use 12–24 month commit examples.
- If security/compliance, lead with Private and audit inclusions; use early statement-of-work to scope nonstandard compliance work.
- If latency/reliability, propose canary Dedicated pool plus automated fallback to hosted (hybrid routing) during ramp.

Objection handling snippets (short scripts):
- “Migration cost is large” => "Pilot-first path: 4–6 week pilot with production traffic caps, we’ll measure unit cost delta and hand back a migration TCO report."
- “We need data residency / HSM” => "Private Enterprise includes KMS/HSM and audit artifacts; we’ll scope SOC2+ evidentiary work in SOW."
- “We can’t stop using hosted” => "Hybrid option: Dedicated pool for critical routes + hosted fallback; same API surface so app changes are minimal."

Playbook Roles & RACI (recommended minimal):
- Account Executive / Commercial Owner: commercial terms, contracting — R
- CS Lead (owner): drive QBR cadence, coordinate pilots — A
- Solutions Engineer: technical feasibility, pilot runbooks — C
- Infra/Platform Eng: internal bridge to delivery org for Dedicated/Private provisioning — C
- Legal/Procure: contract and compliance approvals — I

Operational runbook snippets (working checklist to attach to pilot):
- Week 0: kickoff, define success metrics, access provisioning
- Week 1–2: baseline load testing, KV/prefix caching tuning, quick perf dashboard
- Week 3–4: pilot ingress with 10–30% production traffic, validate p99 targets, iterate prompts and batching
- Week 5–8: scale to steady-state, finalize cutover plan, knowledge transfer

Sample email templates (short) — Outreach after QBR to start pilot:
- Subject: "Pilot proposal: Dedicated pilot to stabilize latency for <Account>"
- Body snippet: "Thanks again for the discussion — attached is a 6-week pilot plan that focuses on the 4 routes causing most latency. Goal: validate p99 latency <X ms and measure per-token cost. Can we target a pilot start on <date>?"

What success looks like (measurable):
- Pilot achieves p99 latency target AND per-token cost improvement or stable cost with improved reliability.
- Contract signature or formal pilot SOW within 30 days of QBR for high-scoring accounts.
- Customer health increases (support tickets down, performance alerts down) and CSAT improves in 90-day post-migration check.

Open questions / outstanding risks (working items):
- Capacity & provisioning lead times for mid-Q spikes — need engineering SLA for Dedicated provisioning during pilots.
- Standard SOW template for compliance-heavy Private deals — legal to deliver draft.
- Pricing guardrails for heavily custom private/on-prem scopes — need finance sign-off on cost-plus thresholds.

Action items (next edits):
- Lina to build a renewable sheet template (lightweight CSV) for renewal + expansion tracker by 2025-03-05.
- Ethan to draft two commercial quote skeletons for Dedicated Basic and Private Starter by 2025-03-07.
- Amir to spin up an internal one-pager for Solutions Engineering with pilot runbook checklist by 2025-03-03.

Notes to self / informal reminders (scratch area):
- Keep messaging focused on "predictable economics" not just raw cost.
- Ask for run-of-the-mill logs for 7 days prior to technical review; saves time.
- Consider a "migration health SLA" pilot incentive (discount if we miss onboarding deadlines).

Attachments to add in final version: pilot-runbook-template.docx, renewal-tracker-template.csv, sample-dedicated-quote.xlsx

Document history: initial draft 2025-02-10, collaborative edits during CS weekly 2025-02-18, outstanding legal input pending 2025-02-28.
